description: The bar chart illustrates the number of participants who selected each criterion when evaluating a generative-AI-driven claim retrieval system, as reported in the paper titled “A Generative-AI-Driven Claim Retrieval System Capable of Detecting and Retrieving Claims from Social Media Platforms in Multiple Languages.” The vertical axis lists seven evaluation criteria: “Relevant FCs,” “FC Summary,” “Relevance Explanation,” “Clarity and Simplicity,” “Overall Summary,” “Filters,” and “Veracity Explanation.” The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Participants,” is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 2. Each criterion is represented by a horizontal bar whose length corresponds to the number of participants selecting it. “Relevant FCs” received the highest selection with 6 participants, followed by “FC Summary” with 5. “Relevance Explanation” and “Clarity and Simplicity” were each selected by 3 participants. “Overall Summary” was chosen by 2 participants, while “Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” were each selected by only 1 participant. The bars are color-coded in shades of gray and green, with darker shades generally corresponding to higher participant counts, and are arranged in descending order from top to bottom based on selection frequency. No error bars, annotations, or additional visual emphasis are present beyond the bar lengths and color differentiation.
